correctness.rationale: All m>=1,r>=2: the hat Gram matrix M=(2dI+A)/6 is derived by exact arclength integration. Direct multiplication verifies every entry of its claimed inverse in three vertex orbit types, with positive denominator. The kernel at a vertex has exactly three edge classes with correct counts and sign patterns. Exact integration gives the rational norm; edgewise affinity reduces global L∞ maximization to vertex rows, and sign(K_v) attains the sharp bound. Algebra proves threshold, finite-difference monotonicity and both limits. The included independent exact Gram inversion and kernel integration check covers 26 instances with 4690 exact assertions. The infinite parameter proof is analytic, not inferred from finite checks. Strict m-monotonicity and the exact m-limit certify the unattained family supremum 7/3.

value.rationale: The problem asks for the natural and practically relevant maximum-norm stability of the canonical arclength least-squares projector on a two-parameter family of regular branched network elements. The complete exact formula, all vertex extremizers, unique threshold m=4 for >2 amplification, positivity defect and distinct asymptotic regimes provide a graph-topology classification not implied by generic conditioning. The result gives a reproducible sharp benchmark for finite-element projection on networks; no downstream major theorem is claimed. Its sharp family supremum 7/3 is approached by balanced complete bipartite graphs with degrees tending to infinity and no pendant vertices.
